leader.name: Quota-boundary workload timing optimizer
leader.state_transition: included or prepaid quota plus reset/expiry boundary -> already-planned non-urgent work exists -> executing on the wrong side of the boundary causes overage or destroys paid allowance -> recommend safe timing/reassignment -> verified incremental spend avoided
leader.why_survived: Fresh research again found many SaaS/API products with non-rollover included allowances and explicit overage billing, including annual e-signature envelope allowances and monthly API/AI/scanning allowances. The trigger is independently generated by billing/usage systems and the financial delta can be measured. Unlike request-routing products, the smallest viable version can stay read-only and recommend timing for already-planned work. No dominant general buyer-side quota-boundary scheduler was found in this run.
strongest_evidence: Current SaaS products continue to expose non-rollover allowances plus overage billing, creating an objective reset boundary.
Docusign terms define annual envelope allowances and per-envelope overage charges, providing a non-AI vertical where quota and financial consequence are explicit.
Security scanning and other SaaS products expose included monthly scans plus per-scan overage, confirming the mechanism beyond AI inference.
Usage dashboards and billing APIs make quota state machine-readable without requiring user-created labels.
leader.closest_threat: The general concept may remain too heterogeneous; individual SaaS products expose their own usage dashboards and first-party spend limits, and the value disappears if workload timing is not safely movable or if the optimizer must sit inline on every request.
leader.smallest_intervention: Read usage/billing APIs or exports plus an existing work queue/calendar; calculate remaining allowance, reset/expiry time, overage rate and job deadlines; recommend RUN BEFORE RESET, DEFER UNTIL RESET, or USE EXISTING ALLOWANCE. No proxy or payment execution initially.
leader.monetization: Small per-success fee or capped percentage of objectively avoided overage/forfeited allowance, calculated from the counterfactual cost of the same already-planned work on the wrong side of the boundary.
leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Need one sufficiently large non-AI vertical with high per-customer leakage, machine-readable work deadlines and enough safe timing flexibility to support repeated savings without request-path ownership.
leader.next_research_test: Narrow the quota-boundary mechanism to enterprise e-signature envelopes, security scanning, communications and other non-AI metered SaaS. Quantify overage economics and test whether existing workflow systems already schedule work against quota boundaries. Promote only a vertical where the queue/deadline data is available and savings recur at meaningful scale.

candidate_updates.reason: Fresh enterprise reconciliation products explicitly surface missing/refund mismatches across gateway, ERP and bank data. The promise-to-settlement recovery layer is still narrower than generic reconciliation, but competitive adjacency is closer than previously scored and aggregate leakage remains unquantified.

The underlying loss is strong: excess earnings credits often expire monthly and examples show material idle balances. However DebtBook explicitly optimizes balances so fees are covered without excess zero-interest cash, bank fee platforms support machine-readable EDI 822/TWIST/CAMT data, and banks themselves offer target-balance sweeps/hybrid accounts that earn interest on excess balances. Gate 8 fails for the obvious implementation.

Core deposits are refundable, deadline-bound and materially lost by repair shops, but current dedicated products and shop-management systems already track every core, deadline, return and credit, including software explicitly marketed around recovering forgotten core deposits.
Cancellation deadlines and no-show penalties are clean machine events, but current corporate travel systems already auto-cancel trips to avoid no-show fees and lost ticket value.
ERP/AP products already track unapplied vendor credits, surface them in payment flows and automatically apply credits before cash payment.

runner_ups.reason: Excellent attribution and non-invasive recovery, but closer reconciliation competition and still-unproven leakage magnitude.
Real app-store recovery/cost tradeoff, but app-wide infrequent configuration and weak performance attribution.
Real expiry but multi-provider routing layers can absorb credit-expiry awareness.

new_search_rules: A large visible leak is not enough if a first-party sweep, target-balance feature or adjacent treasury module already makes the optimal action routine.
Quota-boundary opportunities are stronger when the financial unit and the work unit are both independently machine-readable and the action is merely timing, not routing through our infrastructure.

Before promoting a refundable-deposit or deadline candidate, search vertical operational software; niche industries often already have exact deadline-tracking products even when generic web search suggests whitespace.

When a candidate is a cross-system reconciliation wedge, treat products that already ingest both operational and bank data as stronger Gate-8 threats even if they stop short of performance-priced recovery.
